newsitem.title: UK: Britain poised to ban ownership of most handguns.
newsitem.headline: Britain poised to ban ownership of most handguns.

text.p: The British government is expected to ban ownership of most handguns on Wednesday following an inquiry into the Dunblane massacre in which loner Thomas Hamilton shot dead 16 children and a teacher.
Britain's Channel 4 television reported on Tuesday that the government would also propose a total ban on the ownership of all semi-automatic weapons.
The only exemption to the tough new rules will be small- calibre pistols used in Olympic competitions, according to press reports.
Recommendations made by senior Scottish judge Lord Cullen, who chaired the five-month long inquiry which reported to the government on Monday, will be published on Wednesday.
Prime Minister John Major ordered the inquiry immediately after the Dunblane tragedy, and has pledged to consider legislation to implement any recommendations.
Cullen is not expected to call for a total ban on handguns, but according to newspapers is proposing that owners should have to store them in a secure gun club.
Hamilton, who held firearms certificates issued by the police and was a member of a gun club, used four handguns in the March 13 attack.

The government is expected to go beyond Cullen's recommendations, however. The Guardian newspaper reported on Wednesday that only 0.22 calibre single-shot pistols would be exempted from the government's ban. The pistols, used in Olympic competitions, would have to be kept at gun clubs.
Owners of other handguns would be paid compensation on handing in weapons to the authorities, the Guardian said.
Anti-handgun campaigners have called for a total ban on handgun ownership following Dunblame, and are not likely to be satisfied with a partial ban.
"A complete handgun ban is the only answer to Dunblane," said Ann Pearston, organiser of a petition which has been signed by 750,000 Britons since the tragedy.

"Leave handguns in clubs and a planner like Hamilton will just book them out for a competition or put them in his pocket and walk out," she told the opposition Labour party's annual conference this month.
Britain's Press Association said Labour would call for a total ban on handgun ownership, including Olympic pistols below 0.22 calibre.

Major called a meeting of senior ministers to discuss Cullen's report on Tuesday and Scottish Secretary Michael Forsyth is expected to make a statement to parliament on Wednesday setting out its proposals and giving the government's reaction to them.
Forsyth's own parliamentary constituency includes the small Scottish town of Dunblane.

Britain's gun lobby has run a determined campaign to save the sport of shooting, arguing that what is needed to prevent another Dunblane is a tightening of regulations governing the issue of firearms licences rather than a blanket ban.
It argues that the vast majority of the 57,000 holders of handgun licences practice target shooting and other legitimate activities, and should not suffer because of Hamilton's actions.
